slug: 2020-01-01 Nexus between Civil Registration and Social Protection - Tunisia chapter (IDRC)

facts.fact: The IDRC chapter states that government decree 2016-365 of 18 March 2016 transferred the directorate managing the civil registration system from the Ministry of the Interior to the Ministry of Local Affairs and Environment, which has contracted the Centre National de l'Informatique (CNI) to host the database and run the network for the municipalities.

The IDRC chapter states that each civil status event, in the four registers of births, deaths, marriages and divorces, is handwritten in two copies of the paper register and then transcribed into the computerised system; undated, so dated to the PDF's 2020 publication year.

The IDRC chapter states that civil status facts are recorded directly in the central database by the registrar, after being handwritten in the paper register, and are accessible the next morning throughout the national territory; undated, so dated to the PDF's 2020 publication year.

The IDRC chapter states that by April 2005 the national computerised civil registry system and its database were fully operational, linking all municipalities, some municipalities having started to use it in 2003; no count of offices is given for that date.

The IDRC chapter states that all civil registration offices have interconnected computer systems, that the offices of the recently created municipalities also have the equipment and connections, and that all municipalities have access to Madania; it counts 350 principal offices and 170 subsidiary offices, annexes and mobile units, and gives no number registering; undated, so dated to the PDF's 2020 publication year.
